newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seita weak after U.S. tobacco settlement.
newsitem.headline: Seita weak after U.S. tobacco settlement.

text.p: Shares in cigarette company Seita fell on Monday after the U.S. tobacco industry agreed to pay $368.5 billion as part of a landmark settlement.
Seita shares were down 1.58 percent at 187 francs, underperforming the CAC-40 index, which was 0.23 percent lower at 0850 GMT.
"There's a feeling that governments may develop a common policy toward tobacco," a broker said.
Brokers said tobacco stocks were also pressured by recent falls in U.S. tobacco shares and a growing view that the balance is tipping in favour of anti-smoking groups and regulations.
But some analysts cautioned against drawing too many conclusions.

"Clearly this is bleeding into other markets, but it's wrong to see a settlement in the States as an opportunity to pursue tobacco companies in other countries," one analyst said. "There are big differences in legal structure that make it harder for plaintiffs to pursue the tobacco industry."
The U.S. settlement, which will lead to higher cigarette prices in the United States, boils down to a tax increase, the analyst said.
From that perspective, European companies can argue that they already contribute more, given the higher tax levels in Europe, the analyst added.
Analyst Emilio Alvarez at Morgan Stanley said pre-settlement tax levels in the United States were around 30 percent, compared with 75-80 percent in Europe.
"Product liability is less developed in Europe," he said. For those two reasons, he said he expected the impact of the U.S. settlement on European tobacco stocks to be limited.
Seita, which makes Gitanes and Gauloises cigarettes, had no immediate comment on the settlement.
